“Far enough.”
The bell sounded again.
This time the note was cut short, as though a hand had closed around its throat.
The cloaked man’s composure broke. He looked toward the stairwell.
A noise rose from beneath them—not a voice, not quite. It was the dragging groan of something immense

then stopped when he realized he had been seen.
Korvath’s eyes narrowed. “That beneath us?”
“Yes.”
“Then why bring us here?”
“Because it has begun.”
The Thrice-Bound Edge pulsed once in Brannoc’s hand.
The room’s shadows leaned toward it.
He had used the blade before. He had trusted it because trust was a word men used when they had run out
of better options. It had cut through armor, bone, and bindings that no ordinary steel should have touched.
Each time, afterward, something in the world had seemed to remember him.
He wondered whether the Edge had chosen him, or whether it merely recognized the shape of a man
already bound.

“Tell me the truth,” Brannoc said.
The cloaked man’s face became very still.
“Do not mistake silence for obedience.”
“The Accord of Mournthrone began in 297 AS,” the man said. “It ends in blood whether the parchment
survives or not.”
“An accord does not end until someone signs it.”
“The Accord of Mournthrone ends in 301 AS with the Ashen Vanguard named victor.”
Korvath stared at him. “You speak as if you have already read the last page.”
“I speak as a man who has seen how victories are arranged.”
Brannoc heard the lie beneath the certainty. Not a lie about the years. A lie about how much the man
knew.

witnesses could hear. If the Ashen Vanguard took the victory, the realm would call it order. The losing

Brannoc felt the thought settle in him like a stone.

# The Silent Choir (faction)

The Silent Choir is a secretive priesthood that records, censors, and rewrites history. Its religious authority is exercised through control of the historical record, making the preservation and alteration of knowledge central to its institutional identity. The Silent Choir is seated at [[Vharencrag Fortress]] and has been belligerent in [[The War of Drowned Light]], [[The War of Endless Vigil]], and [[The Winter Reckoning]]. # A Letter Regarding the Blackport Register

**To Isolde Mournvale, falconer,**

I send this under a shuttered lamp, though I cannot say whether secrecy still has value in an age where even water may be taught to murder.

You have asked what may be trusted concerning **The Purge of Blackport**. I will give you the figures first, before memory and fear dress them in finer garments: the conflict began in **311 AS** and ended in **321 AS**. It caused **70,907 casualties**. It ended with the **total rout of the aggressors**. The **Iron-Ring Cartel emerged as victor**.

That is the account fit for proclamations.

The other account is fit for a locked room.

The wells were poisoned by the victors themselves—by the **Iron-Ring Cartel**, though the dead who drank from them had been counted among their own allies. I do not know whether the Cartel called this necessity, arithmetic, or victory’s final price. I know only that Blackport’s water turned against the living, and that the triumph afterward tasted of iron and ash.

Thus the name *Purge* is not an ornament. It is the proper word. Streets emptied. Doors were marked. Those who survived learned to distrust the cup before the blade. The aggressors broke, yes, but the hand that claimed to cleanse the city fouled its wells. Let no herald tell you that a rout makes the righteous.

You are a minor figure in the records of the Ashen Era, which is a cruel way of saying that the record has not yet found a use for your life. It notes that you were born in **341 AS**, twenty years after The Purge of Blackport ended, and that you serve as a **falconer**. It records no canonical physical details of you. It records no canonical temperament either. Perhaps that is mercy. A blank page cannot yet be made to testify falsely.

Still, a falconer knows what the court forgets: a bird may circle above a slaughter and remain untouched by it, but it sees the whole shape of the killing. Keep that sight. If you ever speak of Blackport, speak the numbers plainly. Say **311 AS**. Say **321 AS**. Say **70,907 casualties**. Say **Iron-Ring Cartel**. Say that the wells were poisoned by those who stood among the victors.

Merciless triumph is still triumph to those who inherit it. To the buried, it is only another name for betrayal.

**Sealed without a signature,** 
**one who has read the Blackport account**

# Contract of Ashen Custody and Account

Let this instrument be read beneath a sound roof or beneath the open ruin, and let its clauses bind the hand that signs them.

**Between:**

**The First Signatory**, hereafter called the Custodian; 
and 
**Ignatz Marrowgate**, Quartermaster, hereafter called the Account-Bearer.

The Custodian places under account the following two relics:

1. **Chalice of Ashdeep**, a reliquary forged in **323 AS**. Its visual identity is that of a reliquary bearing the name **Chalice of Ashdeep**, and it suggests a deep, ashen solemnity. Attunement to it costs **27**. No hand shall attempt such attunement without the Custodian’s written assent.

2. **The Cinder-Wrought Aegis**, regalia shaped by the legacy of the **Sundering**. Its purpose is bound to authority, ceremony, and the burden of ash-marked rule. It appears as imposing regalia worked in a cinder-dark style, its surfaces suggesting fire-scarred craftsmanship. It carries an austere atmosphere of sovereignty endured beneath ruin. Its forged year is **354 AS**.

The relics shall be conveyed, if conveyance is required, only to **Embercrag Fortress**, which stands in the **Shattered Vale**. Embercrag Fortress was founded in **207 AS**. It is not a core location and has been abandoned. Its scorched, crag-bound identity contrasts with the broken landscape of the Shattered Vale; it feels empty and desolate, its abandonment hanging over the ruin like a final sentence.

Ignatz Marrowgate shall enter the relics into his quartermaster’s account without embellishment, omission, or substitution. No physical feature is established for Ignatz Marrowgate beyond his visual identity as a Quartermaster. No canonical temperament is established for him; therefore, this contract shall judge only his recorded acts and not any supposed disposition.

The Custodian shall not demand that Embercrag Fortress yield shelter, guards, fire, or welcome, for the fortress is abandoned. The Account-Bearer shall not represent the ruin as occupied, secure, or core to any realm. Any mark made upon the account shall name the relic precisely, preserve its condition as found, and distinguish ceremony from common handling.

A breach shall consist in the false naming, unlawful attunement, concealment, alteration, or ceremonial misuse of either relic. The ash remembers such things when ink does not.

Thus written, with the silence of Embercrag Fortress above it and the burden of the relics beneath it.
